## Appendix: the tests on past forecasts {#sec-appendix-backtest .appendix}

```{python}
st = D.TRAJ["backtest"]["statutory"]
tr = st["treatments"]
def block(t):
    return tr[t]["chronological"]
origins = block("published")["origins"]
def ranges(t):
    return {k: v for k, v in block(t)["methods"].items() if k != "obr_point"}
def best(t):
    rs = ranges(t)
    b = max(v["burnham_2030_inside"] for v in rs.values())
    leader = min((k for k, v in rs.items() if v["burnham_2030_inside"] == b), key=lambda k: rs[k]["burnham_2030_crps_pp"])
    missed = [o for o, hit in zip(origins, rs[leader]["burnham_2030_inside_by_origin"]) if not hit]
    return b, leader, missed
b_pub, lead_pub, _ = best("published")
b_law, lead_law, missed_law = best("suspended")
small = [k for k, v in ranges("published").items() if v["max_draws"] < 10]
windows = st["origin_april_upratings"]
all_under = all(v["switches_expected"] < v["switches_realised"] for v in ranges("published").values())
assert all(spike["year"] in windows[o] for o in missed_law)
```

This appendix gives the scores behind the screen of @sec-screen, then an earlier, wider backtest kept as the record.

@tbl-screen gives the dry-run scores of the screen on today's inputs, for each of the five forms in tests A and B. April 2022 is scored as the law applied it (earnings set equal to CPI), which decides the verdict, and as published, which is reported beside it and has no say. Coverage is the share of outcomes inside the form's central 80% band: of the yearly gaps between earnings and CPI ("annual") and of the gap the two rules open after four rises ("final years"). The biases are the form's mean minus what happened: in the yearly gap (percentage points), in the number of changes of lead per path, and in the share of years with earnings below the floor. A form must pass every condition in both tests; the verdict column gives the screen's result for the form as a whole.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-screen
#| tbl-cap: "The screen's dry-run scores on today's inputs: coverage of the central 80% band and biases, by test, form and treatment of April 2022. The verdict uses April 2022 as in law; the published treatment is shown for reference only."
scr = D.R["uncertainty_screen"]
FORM_NAMES = {"monthly_var1_boot": "Monthly model (used here)", "monthly_var2_boot": "Monthly model, two lags",
              "monthly_var1_tcop": "Monthly model, Student-t shocks", "monthly_var1_gauss": "Monthly model, Gaussian shocks",
              "annual_boot_gap": "Annual model plus past gaps"}
TREAT = {"suspended": "As in law", "published": "As published"}
body = []
for test in ("A", "B"):
    for form, verdict in scr["c2_outcome"]["forms"].items():
        for t in ("suspended", "published"):
            r = scr["c2_scores"]["scores"][test][t][form]
            body.append([test, FORM_NAMES.get(form, form), TREAT[t],
                         ("Pass" if verdict["passes"] else "Fail") if t == "suspended" else "Reference",
                         pct(100 * r["annual_gap_coverage"]["mean"], 0),
                         f'{r["terminal_coverage"]["hits"]} of {r["terminal_scored_origins"]}',
                         num(r["gap_bias_pp"]["mean"], 2), num(r["switch_bias"]["mean"], 2), num(r["floor_bias"]["mean"], 2)])
display(Markdown(md_table(["Test", "Form", "April 2022", "Verdict", "Annual coverage", "Final years inside",
                           "Gap bias", "Lead-change bias", "Floor-share bias"], body, "lllrrrrrr")))
```

Before that screen we ran a wider backtest, kept here as the earlier record. It is why the paper reports an expected value and scenarios, not the probability of any outcome. We scored `{python} words(len(ranges("published")))` ways of putting a range on the two statutory inputs, and the OBR forecast alone, against what followed `{python} words(len(origins))` OBR forecasts (the `{python} origins[0]` to the `{python} origins[-1]`): the forecasts with at least two earlier forecasts whose target years had all been published, which the method built on past forecast errors needs. Each method is fitted only on data dated before the forecast, using today's revised figures, and scored on the September CPI and May–July earnings for the `{python} words(H)` years after the forecast year, which set the April rises two to five years after it.

The scores are proper scoring rules [@gneiting2007]: the continuous ranked probability score (CRPS) for the gap between the triple lock and the Burnham plan after those rises, in points of the pension; the energy score for the two series over the years together; and the variogram score [@scheuerer2015], which rewards getting the dependence between years right. Lower is better for each. We also record whether the realised gap fell inside each method's middle 80%, and how many changes of lead between CPI and earnings the method expected against how many happened.

@tbl-appendix gives each method's score for the gap and its coverage, with April 2022 scored both ways; how April 2022 is scored decides the result. Scored on the published May–July 2021 earnings growth of `{python} rate(tr["published"]["april_2022_inputs"]["earnings"])`, `{python} "every method expected fewer changes of lead than happened, and " if all_under else ""`the best placed `{python} words(b_pub)` of `{python} words(len(origins))` realised gaps in its middle 80%. Scored with earnings equal to CPI (`{python} rate(tr["suspended"]["april_2022_inputs"]["cpi"])`) that April, as the law set it when the earnings leg was suspended, the best placed `{python} words(b_law)` of `{python} words(len(origins))`; the best-scoring of those (`{python} lower1(D.STATUTORY_LABELS[lead_law])`) missed the `{python} listing(missed_law)` forecasts, whose rises include April `{python} spike["year"]`, set by September CPI of `{python} rate(spike["cpi"])`. The method built on `{python} listing([lower1(D.STATUTORY_LABELS[k]) for k in small])` has only `{python} min(ranges("published")[k]["min_draws"] for k in small)`–`{python} max(ranges("published")[k]["max_draws"] for k in small)` paths at these forecasts, so its middle 80% is the full range of those paths. Neither treatment gives a reliable 80% range, so we report at most an expected saving, and only from a model that passes the screen of @sec-screen. The spread across paths we describe as scenarios.

```{python}
#| label: tbl-appendix
#| tbl-cap: "The forecast-distribution backtest over the chronological OBR forecasts, with April 2022 scored as published and as in law: CRPS of the gap after the rises (points of the pension); how many realised gaps fell inside the method's middle 80%; the energy score and the variogram score over the same series in different years; and changes of lead, predicted against actual. Lower scores are better."
pubm, lawm = block("published")["methods"], block("suspended")["methods"]
body = []
for k, label in D.STATUTORY_SHORT.items():
    a, l = pubm[k], lawm[k]
    point = k == "obr_point"
    body.append([label, num(a["burnham_2030_crps_pp"], 2), "n/a" if point else a["burnham_2030_inside"],
                 num(l["burnham_2030_crps_pp"], 2), "n/a" if point else l["burnham_2030_inside"],
                 num(a["energy"], 2), num(a["vs_serial"], 2), f'{num(a["switches_expected"], 1)} / {num(a["switches_realised"], 1)}'])
display(Markdown(md_table(["Method", "Gap CRPS, published", "Inside", "Gap CRPS, in law", "Inside",
                           "Energy, published", "Variogram, published", "Lead changes, published"], body)))
```
